newsitem.title: TURKEY: U.S.-sponsored Kurds leave Iraq for Turkey.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-sponsored Kurds leave Iraq for Turkey.

text.p: Hundreds of Kurds who worked for U.S.-affiliated organisations have been evacuated to Turkey from Iraq amid the latest Kurdish infighting in northern Iraq, Turkish border officials said on Sunday.

Around 700 Kurds, including relatives, poured through the Habur border crossing overnight on their way to a temporary camp in the Turkish town of Silopi. Turkish customs officers and two U.S. officials questioned them on their arrival, witnesses said.
Washington last month evacuated more than 2,000 Kurds who had worked for U.S. military, aid and intelligence programmes in northern Iraq after Baghdad intervened in the Kurdish fighting last month.
Clashes between two rival Kurdish factions erupted again last week when the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) tried to retake territory lost last month to the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).

In late August the KDP captured the regional capital of Arbil with backing from Iraqi government troops and then took control of the whole of the Kurdish north. There has been no sign of Baghdad's involvement this time.
